hypothesis: R257's realized P&L was dominated by repeated strength winners. A 5-day reversal weakest link should retain quality and industry-relative leadership while avoiding names that have just become short-term overextended, broadening the set of executable leaders without changing R257's internal formula or portfolio constraints.
selection_basis: R257 passed all predictive, return and cost-stress gates but failed C2/C3/C4 with top1/top3/top5 net P&L shares of 27.95%/64.08%/94.43%. R258's 20-day re-entry gate was rejected before returns because its daily fresh-name median was only one. R259 changes the economic dimension rather than tuning R257 or R258: it adds 5-day short-term reversal as a second weak link while keeping R257's formula, holding period, stop loss, score-pool size, position count and cost assumptions unchanged. Feasibility read no forward or strategy returns: joint coverage is 99.9211% full, 99.9646% discovery, 99.8797% validation and 99.9122% recent year; 42 month-end component rank correlations have mean absolute 0.219068 and maximum absolute 0.515145; the composite is 0.185805 lower than the R257 percentile on average and is at least 0.10 lower for 41.1718% of observations; the minimum daily valid candidate count is 246. Evidence: r259_data_feasibility.json.

factor.formula: quality_rs_pullback_min_rank = min(rank_pct(quality_relative_strength_min_rank), rank_pct(-momentum_5d)) within same-date historical nonfinancial HS300 members; 1 is best and 0 is worst

component_definitions.quality_relative_strength_min_rank: R257 composite of the R253 quality weakest link and same-date 20-day stock-relative-to-industry strength
component_definitions.reversal_5d: -(close_t / close_t_minus_5_trading_days - 1), using front-adjusted closes through date t

factor.interpretation: R257 remains unchanged. R259 requires both quality-relative leadership and the absence of a sharp recent five-day extension.
factor.pit_rule: R257 inherits its financial publication/PIT dates and same-date industry-relative strength. momentum_5d uses front-adjusted closes through date t. Ranks and the minimum use only same-date eligible historical nonfinancial HS300 members.
factor.missing_data_rule: Both components are required; a missing component leaves the composite null.

strategies.common_filter: Current nonfinancial industry snapshot is required; history uses historical HS300 membership. Both strategies require ma60 and non-null quality_rs_pullback_min_rank so the candidate and control universe is identical. The R257 factor and its two underlying component fields are also declared as required features for auditability.
strategies.execution: 30-name score limit, at most 10 equal-weight positions, 20-day holding, -20% stop loss, T+1 open execution and 3x costs; candidate also tested at 4x/5x.

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally

segments.stitching: compound two independently run segment curves; skip the first return of each later segment

factor_ic.method: R259 factor month-end rank IC versus T+1 open to T+21 open return within historical nonfinancial HS300 members

gates.D1: full and recent-12-month joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D2: discovery and validation joint component coverage >=0.99
gates.D3: first valid date is no later than 2023-05-04 and written values exactly match the same-date composite formula with max abs difference <=1e-12
gates.D4: mean absolute monthly component correlation <=0.70, every monthly absolute correlation <=0.80, mean composite reduction versus R257 percentile >=0.05 and at least 20% of observations reduced by >=0.10
gates.I1: discovery mean R259 rank IC >=0.02 with at least 18 month-end observations
gates.I2: validation mean R259 rank IC >=0.01 with at least 18 month-end observations and the same positive sign
gates.G2: discovery candidate MDD is no worse than control MDD by more than 5pp
gates.G4: full-sample candidate return > 0 and >= control return
gates.G5: full-sample candidate MDD <= 40% in absolute value and no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G6: rolling 1-year positive rate >= 60% and no worse than control by more than 2pp
gates.G7: recent 12-month candidate return > 0 and MDD no worse than control by more than 5pp
gates.G8: full-sample candidate return at 4x cost is positive
gates.G9: full-sample candidate return at 5x cost is positive
gates.C1: at least 30 distinct symbols are traded across the full sample
gates.C2: the largest symbol's share of net P&L is <= 25%
gates.C3: the top three symbols' share of net P&L is <= 55%
gates.C4: the top five symbols' share of net P&L is <= 75%
gates.C5: at least 8 distinct symbols have positive P&L in the validation segment
gates.C6: the largest industry's share of gross profit is <= 45%
gates.C7: the largest single-symbol loss is <= 20% of gross profit in absolute value

decision_rule: All D, I, G and C gates must pass. Any failure means the quality-relative-strength plus 5-day-reversal factor is not accepted and cannot be rescued by changing component weights, reversal window, rank direction, holding period, stop loss, universe, costs or gates after seeing results.
known_limitations: The 5-day reversal component can be noisy, increase turnover and conflict with momentum persistence.
The minimum of two percentile ranks can be sparse and sensitive to ties.
R253, industry-relative strength and price reversal were already researched in overlapping samples, so multiple-comparison risk remains.
The nonfinancial industry snapshot is current rather than historical PIT.
R253 inherits financial restatement and publication-timing risk.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments and segment boundaries can reset open positions.
Passing these gates would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
